title: boardsmith.json
description: Single source of truth for the set of top-level keys a boardsmith.json project config may legitimately carry. `src/cli/lib/config-schema.ts` derives ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS from `Object.keys(properties)` below, and `boardsmith validate` / `boardsmith dev` startup use that list to reject unknown/misspelled keys with a did-you-mean suggestion. Do NOT add a key here unless it has a real read site: either a command in src/cli/commands consumes it (see the file:line trace in 135-05-PLAN.md's read_first), or the PUBLISHING PLATFORM consumes it out of the manifest that build.ts's deriveManifest produces by spreading this config. The platform has two manifest sinks, and reaching either one takes MORE than listing a key here. (1) The Convex sink, which is what platform-level flags like `asyncPlay` are read from (`convex/games.ts` `parseAsyncPlayFlag`): `convex/publish.ts` `initiatePublishServer` stores verbatim what it is SENT, but what it is sent is an allow-list projection built by `buildInitiateManifest` in `src/cli/lib/publish-api.ts` — a key absent from that function never arrives, silently, however well it is declared here. (2) The R2 sink the runtime session host reads: the bundle zip carries `dist/manifest.json` whole, and the games worker rebuilds an R2 copy through its own allowlist (`games/src/manifest-schema.ts`), silently dropping keys that allowlist does not name. So a key needs a named reader on at least one sink AND a place on that sink's forwarding list; a key only the Convex sink carries is invisible to the runtime session host by design. EVERY property below therefore carries a REQUIRED `x-convex-sink` boolean saying whether sink (1) consumes it AS A TOP-LEVEL KEY. A key marked false is not necessarily invisible to the platform: `asyncPlay` and `joinInProgress` reach it inside the DERIVED `capabilities` object that `build.ts` resolves (#171) and `publish-api.ts` forwards explicitly, exactly as `playerCount` is forwarded, and a derived key is not an authorable property so it is not listed here at all. `config-schema.ts` derives CONVEX_SINK_KEYS from it and `buildInitiateManifest` forwards exactly that set, so `marked true but not forwarded` cannot be written; `validate.test.ts` refuses a property that declares neither, so `added and never decided` cannot be committed. Sink (2)'s allowlist lives in another repository and is NOT expressible here — do not add a second annotation claiming to govern it.

$schema.description: Optional editor schema reference (point it at this file's $id for IDE autocomplete/validation). Ignored by the CLI — this is the one key exempt from the read-site rule above, because the schema itself can only be consumed through it.

backend.description: WHICH BACKEND RUNS THIS GAME, and the only place it is declared. `table` holds the whole element tree resident, snapshots per action, and keeps history, undo, bots and spectators; `world` keeps only named partitions resident, checkpoints what a command dirtied, and runs continuously. Same engine, same element tree, same action system, different storage and checkpoint policy. Required, because a default would be a backend nobody chose. It is declared HERE rather than derived from the compiled rules because `boardsmith dev` has to know which host to start before it loads any rules -- but a declaration that contradicts the code is refused: `boardsmith build` and `boardsmith validate` both check it against `gameDefinition.world` (see src/session/capabilities.ts). What the choice IMPLIES is not written here or anywhere else by hand: build resolves it into the manifest's `capabilities` object, and every reader -- the shell, the CLI, the publishing platform -- reads that object rather than this name.

audience.description: Who the game is for — exactly one platform shelf. The canonical value list lives on the platform (GET /api/taxonomy); `boardsmith publish` preflight-validates against it. Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

tags.description: Freeform discovery tags (mechanisms, themes, eras) — e.g. 'abstract', 'worker-placement', 'family-friendly'. Normalized server-side. Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

playtime.description: Estimated play time range in minutes (min <= max). Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

cooperative.description: True when players win or lose together. A structural fact synced to the platform on every publish. Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

thumbnail.description: Relative path to the game's thumbnail image, resolved from the project root. NOT scaffold-emitted: `boardsmith new` creates no thumbnail image, so declaring the key by default meant every new game named a file its bundle did not carry. `boardsmith validate` fails when a declared asset path resolves to nothing (`x-asset-path` marks which keys it checks).

gameOptions.description: Game-level option definitions surfaced in the dev host and lobby. Read by dev.ts.

playerOptions.description: Per-player option definitions surfaced in the dev host and lobby. Read by dev.ts.

colorPalette.description: Custom per-player color choices. Read by dev.ts.

paths.description: Optional overrides for the rules/ui source directories (paths.rules, paths.ui). Read by dev.ts, simulate.ts, evolve-bot-weights.ts.

gameId.description: Stable platform game identifier, written back into boardsmith.json by `boardsmith publish` after first publish. Read by publish.ts.

publisher.description: Publisher slug, written back into boardsmith.json by `boardsmith publish` (from --publisher). Read by publish.ts.

publisherId.description: Stable platform publisher identifier, written back into boardsmith.json by `boardsmith publish`. Read by publish.ts.

joinInProgress.description: May a player join a session that is already underway? Absence is the 'no' answer; only a game whose rules can seat a latecomer (a dormant-seat design) should set it. TABLE BACKEND ONLY: a world is always joinable in progress, so the world backend already answers this and writing it on a world is refused (#171). Reaches the platform inside the manifest's derived `capabilities` object.

asyncPlay.description: May this game be played asynchronously -- one move at a time, over hours or days, with nobody else connected? Absence is the 'no' answer; only a game whose rules survive long gaps between moves should set it. TABLE BACKEND ONLY: a world is always asynchronous, so the world backend already answers this and writing it on a world is refused (#171). Reaches the platform inside the manifest's derived `capabilities` object.

idleAction.description: The action the platform submits on behalf of a seat whose round deadline expired, for a game that ships no bot. Required by the platform alongside `roundDeadline` when `bot` is not true. Consumed by the platform (manifest-schema.ts `idleAction`).

defaultHours.description: Used by a table that expresses no preference. Must satisfy minHours <= defaultHours <= maxHours.

minHours.description: Floor a table may choose. The platform's own floor is 1 hour.

maxHours.description: Ceiling a table may choose. The platform's own ceiling is 720 hours (30 days).

mindingSafe.description: The author's explicit acknowledgement that a caretaker bot may play an absent player's seat in THIS game. The platform requires it when `bot: true` resolves an expiry.

roundDeadline.description: How long one round may sit before the platform intervenes. Consumed by the platform (manifest-schema.ts `roundDeadline`), which also enforces its own hour bounds and requires either `bot: true` or an `idleAction` alongside it.

name.description: The action name, exactly as the game's rules register it.

args.description: Optional literal arguments submitted with the action. Opaque to the platform — what constitutes a legal action is the game's business.

namedAction.description: An action the PLATFORM submits on a game's behalf, named as the game's rules register it.
